parameters.content:
### Human handoff setup
1. Replace the URL in **Request Human Handoff** with your real Blueflow install, e.g.
   `https://yourapp.com/api/widget/conversations`
2. Replace the `X-Webhook-Secret` header value with the same secret as `N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in Blueflow's `.env`.
3. This branch only fires when the model emits `HANDOFF:REQUESTED` (see the system prompt built in **Build RAG Prompt**).
4. Laravel matches the visitor to an agent automatically (least-busy, active agents only) and notifies them - this workflow just needs to report the handoff and hand back `conversationId`/`lastMessageId` so the widget starts polling for the agent's replies.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ client_id: $json.clientId, session_token: $json.sessionToken, name: $json.appointmentDetails.name, scheduled_at: $json.appointmentDetails.scheduled_at, reason: $json.appointmentDetails.reason || null }) }}

parameters.content:
### Appointment booking setup
1. Replace the URL in **Book Appointment** with your real Blueflow install, e.g.
   `https://yourapp.com/api/widget/appointments`
2. Replace the `X-Webhook-Secret` header value with the same secret as `N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in Blueflow's `.env` (same secret used by the handoff branch above).
3. This branch only fires when the model emits `APPOINTMENT:BOOK {...}` with a real name + date/time (see the system prompt built in **Build RAG Prompt**).
4. Laravel always replies 200 with a `status` field (`success`, `conflict`, `limit_reached`, or `unavailable`) rather than an HTTP error, specifically so this branch can read back a graceful message to the visitor instead of the request just failing silently — e.g. if that exact date/time is already booked for someone else, or the business has hit its plan's appointment limit for this billing period.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ client_id: $json.clientId, session_token: $json.sessionToken, intent: $json.leadDetails.intent, budget: $json.leadDetails.budget || null, timeline: $json.leadDetails.timeline || null }) }}

parameters.content:
### Lead qualification setup
1. Replace the URL in **Capture Lead** with your real Blueflow install, e.g.
   `https://yourapp.com/api/widget/lead`
2. Replace the `X-Webhook-Secret` header value with the same secret used by the other two branches above.
3. This branch fires when the model emits `LEAD:QUALIFIED {...}` after naturally picking up on what the visitor is interested in (see the system prompt built in **Build RAG Prompt**) - it never interrogates the visitor with a checklist.
4. Laravel flags the matching Customer record as a qualified lead with the captured intent/budget/timeline and notifies the client's users (once per customer, not on every re-mention) - visible under Customers in their dashboard. Subject to the plan's lead-qualification limit, same as appointments and messages.
